topic: Unlocking the Beauty of Euler's Formula: e^(πi) = -1
target_audience: High school students or curious learners with basic knowledge of trigonometry and complex numbers.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Complex Plane
lecture_lines: The complex plane has real and imaginary axes.
Think of points as coordinates on a map.
A point like 3+2i is easily plotted.
animations: Create a complex plane with real (x) and imaginary (y) axes in #FFFFFF. Label 'Re' and 'Im' in #FFFF00.
Plot the point 3+2i at coordinate (3,2). Highlight with a circle in #00FF00.
Display the label '3+2i' near the point in #00FF00.

sections.title: The Meaning of i and Rotation
lecture_lines: Multiplying by 'i' rotates numbers ninety degrees.
This movement forms a perfect circle.
animations: Display the number 1 on the real axis in #FFFFFF. Rotate it 90 degrees CCW by multiplying by i.
Show the point at 0+i (i). Repeat the rotation to land at -1. Highlight in #FF00FF.
Draw a circle connecting 1, i, -1, -i to visualize the continuous rotation. Use #FF00FF.

sections.title: Introducing the Taylor Series (The Engine)
lecture_lines: Complex functions can be infinite sums.
Taylor series use simple powers as building blocks.
Stacking these blocks creates complex shapes.
animations: Display the power terms: 1, x, x^2/2!, x^3/3!. Color in #00FFFF.
Show how these terms 'stack' linearly to form a path. Animate them appearing one by one.
Transform these simple terms into the exponential series curve. Use #FFA500 for the final shape.

sections.title: The Euler Identity Derivation
lecture_lines: Series expansions of e^x, cos, and sin link.
Replacing x with ix merges these series.
Euler's formula connects exponentials to rotation.
This creates cos(x) plus i times sin(x).
animations: Display the infinite series for e^x, cos(x), and sin(x) side by side in #FFFFFF.
Replace x with ix in the series. Highlight the changed signs in #FF0000.
Show the resulting series re-grouping into cos(x) and i*sin(x). Highlight re-grouped parts in #00FF00.
Animate the point on the unit circle moving as x increases. Use #FFFF00 for the circle.
Overlay the identity e^(ix) = cos(x) + i*sin(x) in #FFFFFF, centered.

sections.title: The Grand Finale: e^(πi) = -1
lecture_lines: Set the input x to pi.
Rotation of pi radians reaches the left side.
The result is exactly negative one.
e to the pi i is negative one.
animations: Highlight point at 1 on the real axis. Color in #FFFFFF.
Animate rotation of the point around the circle by angle pi. Use #FF0000.
Show the point arriving at -1 on the real axis. Flash point in #00FF00.
Display 'e^(πi) = -1' prominently in the center. Use #FFFF00.
Highlight all terms of the final identity with a pulsing white box.
